newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - firm 1/8 in quiet activity.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - firm 1/8 in quiet activity.

text.p: U.S. municipal bond prices were assessed from flat to around 1/8 of a point higher in early talk, buoyed by firmer Treasuries, but there was little secondary market activity, making assessments difficult.

"We're just heating up here, right now," a trader said, explaining the market was digesting the latest round of data, a surprising fall in October's U.S. trade gap and a slim rise in initial unemployment claims, which helped support prices.
A surge in overseas sales of aircraft narrowed the U.S. trade gap to $7.99 billion, the lowest deficit in seven months, and down sharply from the $10.4 billion gap that had been forecast.
Weekly jobless claims rose 1,000 to 351,000 for the week ended December 14, though this gain was less than a predicted rise of as much as 14,000.

Despite the early lift provided by these economic reports, traders noted that among the potential factors that could restrain prices from moving higher was the circulation of at least a few bid lists.
"There seems to be some selling of index bonds, there are a couple of bid lists out," a trader said.

This factor also was seen on Wednesday, when the premium enjoyed by the December municipal futures traded on the Chicago Board of Trade over the Bond Buyer's 40-bond index fell sharply in late trade. Traders cited liquidation pressure ahead of the March futures expiry at Thursday's session close.
They also noted that since June, when the 40-bond index strongly outperformed the overall market, players have been wary of shorting the municipal contracts.

The March municipal bond futures firmed six ticks to 115-4/32, while the March U.S. Treasury futures gained seven ticks to 112-9/32. This left the MOB spread between the two futures contracts at plus 91 ticks.

Municipal bond sales are expected to total $207 million, with $76 million of competitive issues, comprised of 10 offerings. The largest is a $17 million New Rochelle School District, N.Y., offering at 1100 EST.
Negotiated sales, which total $130 million in four offerings, include a $75 million Alabama IDA revenue bond sale through JP Morgan Securities.
New York City's $626 million of general obligations, which were sold on Tuesday, were freed to trade as of 0930 EST.

In the secondary market, actively quoted issues included Florida State Board of Education Capital Outlay Public Education of June 2026, which pay a 5-1/2 percent coupon, and were bid at 5.72 percent NET, unchanged.
And North Carolina Eastern Municipal Power Agency Power System Revenues of January 2024, which have a 5-5/8 percent coupon, were bid at 98-1/8, up 3/8 of a point.
